skill.name: emil-design-eng
skill.description: Applies Emil Kowalski's design engineering principles to UI polish, component interactions, animation choices, performance, and accessibility.
skill.summary: Review and refine interface motion, interaction details, component behavior, and perceived performance with practical design engineering guidance.

content.user_title: Polish Interfaces with Design Engineering Principles
content.value_statement: Interface details can feel inconsistent, slow, or visually disconnected. This skill applies practical motion, interaction, performance, and accessibility guidance to improve UI polish.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI code using a Before, After, and Why markdown table.
Recommends animation timing, easing, and when frequent interactions should avoid motion.
Suggests CSS, Motion, spring, gesture, tooltip, popover, drawer, toast, and button patterns.
Identifies performance concerns involving animated properties, CSS variables, and main-thread animation.
Applies reduced-motion guidance and touch-safe hover behavior.
Guides animation debugging through slow motion, frame inspection, and real-device testing.
limitations: The skill provides guidance but cannot visually inspect an interface without host-provided browser or image tools.
Its recommendations reflect one design philosophy and may conflict with an established brand or design system.
Browser support and library behavior must be verified for the target environment.
Timing and easing values are starting points that require testing with real content and devices.

use_cases.title: Review a Frontend Component
use_cases.description: Find motion, feedback, accessibility, and performance issues in a component before release.

use_cases.title: Define Product Motion
use_cases.description: Create consistent animation rules for common interactions across a product interface.

use_cases.title: Refine a Component Library
use_cases.description: Improve default behavior for buttons, tooltips, popovers, drawers, toasts, and gestures.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this button interaction. It scales on press and uses a 300ms animation. Identify the highest-impact improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants focused feedback on one component.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Component Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the following component code using a Before, After, and Why markdown table. Focus on easing, duration, transform origin, hover behavior, and reduced motion: [paste code]
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer wants a structured implementation review.

prompt_templates.title: Design Motion Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Design motion behavior for [component or workflow], used [frequency]. Recommend what should animate, timing, easing, interruptibility, accessibility, and the performance approach.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product team is defining interaction behavior before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Interaction System
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit buttons, tooltips, popovers, drawers, toasts, and drag gestures. Prioritize issues by user impact. Explain tradeoffs and propose one cohesive motion specification: [paste requirements]
prompt_templates.scenario: A design system team needs a broad, advanced motion review.

output_examples.input: Review a dropdown that opens with ease-in over 400ms and scales from zero.
output: Replace the slow entry with a shorter ease-out transition for immediate feedback.
Begin near full size with reduced opacity so the dropdown keeps visual continuity.
Use the trigger position as the transform origin.

output_examples.input: Recommend animation behavior for a command palette opened many times each day.
output_examples.output: Open and close the palette without animation. Frequent keyboard actions should respond immediately and avoid repeated visual delay.

output_examples.input: Audit a draggable drawer that stops abruptly and ignores reduced-motion settings.
output: Add progressive damping beyond the drawer boundary to avoid a hard stop.
Capture the active pointer and ignore additional touches during the drag.
Remove position motion when reduced motion is enabled while preserving useful opacity feedback.

best_practices: Provide component code, interaction frequency, target devices, and product context.
Test proposed motion with real content, reduced-motion settings, touch input, and slower hardware.
Use the recommendations as measurable hypotheses, then compare perceived speed and task completion.
anti_patterns: Do not add animation only for decoration to frequently repeated actions.
Do not apply timing values without checking the product personality and interaction purpose.
Do not treat animation guidance as a substitute for browser compatibility and accessibility testing.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews motion, interaction feedback, component behavior, perceived performance, gesture details, and animation accessibility.

faq.question: Does it generate complete components?
faq.answer: It can recommend implementation patterns and revisions, but complete output depends on the code and framework context provided.

faq.question: Which animation technologies does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CSS transitions, CSS keyframes, Motion springs, the Web Animations API, transforms, clip paths, and gesture logic.

faq.question: Can it review an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide representative components, motion tokens, accessibility requirements, and usage frequency for each interaction.

faq.question: How does it handle reduced motion?
faq.answer: It recommends removing movement that can cause discomfort while preserving useful opacity and color transitions.

faq.question: Are its timing recommendations universal?
faq.answer: No. They are practical starting points that should be tested against product context, device performance, and user expectations.
